title: The Great Morning Football Draft
synopsis: A chaotic family morning unfolds as Tigger bounces around waking everyone up, an argument breaks out over strawberry cake versus honey pie, and various siblings and toys try to sleep in. Once the household is (mostly) up, the kids scramble to pick teams for a backyard football game, complete with a disorganized draft and squabbling over who gets picked first. It's less about the game itself and more about the very real sibling logistics of getting everyone out of bed and onto the field.

title: The Hotline Call About Makuta
synopsis: A frantic call comes in on the emergency hotline: Makuta has escaped, and this time he might actually be able to beat the Super Family. The narrator suits up in battle boots, rallies the team, and heads to Makuta's lair, where the heroes are trapped in a basket before turning the tables. After a string of one-on-one mask battles, the heroes freeze and defeat Makuta and lock him away, at least for now.

title: Pohatu's Gold Mask Showdown
synopsis: The Toa brothers introduce themselves one by one before diving into a rowdy round of mask-battle combat, complete with lost heads, swapped masks, and plenty of trash talk. Pohatu shows off a "super powerful hammer" and switches to a gold mask for extra defense, while Makuta boasts about having six lives to the heroes' one. The fight escalates into a full brawl as masks fly off and lives run out on both sides.

title: Makuta's Return and the Bohrok Hunt
synopsis: After the narrator declares victory and bids the "super family" goodbye, the tone flips: Makuta reveals he's escaped his prison and is already plotting his next conquest. Rather than go after the heroes directly, he decides to hunt down and enslave the six elemental Bohrok one by one, starting with the Fire Bohrok, while back home the family worries about how to stop him for good. A rare stretch told partly from the villain's point of view.

title: The Bohrok Kaita Rises
synopsis: Makuta continues his cross-country search for the remaining Bohrok, scaling mountains and swinging through jungle vines (including an improvised "Tarzan move") to track down Galak, the last one needed. Once all six are gathered, they combine into one giant Bohrok Kaita robot to confront Makuta directly, and the two sides face off in a tense standoff right before the fighting starts.

title: Battle for Makuta's Middle Form
synopsis: The newly combined Bohrok Kaita takes the fight to Makuta, knocking off his first form's masks one by one until he's forced to reveal a tougher "middle part." The Bohrok keep cycling through their own Krana powers looking for an opening, trading taunts about who's really the weakling as the battle grinds on round after round.

title: The Super Family Awards Show
synopsis: The Bohrok finally finish off Makuta for good, and the episode pivots straight into a full awards ceremony, with Dr. Senora and a very literal talking Aku Aku mask hosting and inducting each Toa and Bohrok into the Super Family one by one. Half the fun is the medals not fitting anyone's neck, and the segment wraps with a tongue-in-cheek fake commercial break plugging a trip to Kmart. A silly, earnest victory lap capping off the first movie.

title: Please Visit Our Website
synopsis: A brief, almost entirely wordless interstitial stretch. The only audio is a repeated title-card-style line urging viewers to visit a website, most likely playing over blank tape or a fade between segments rather than any actual scene, so there's essentially no narrated action to summarize here.

title: Turn the Music Down
synopsis: A quiet household stretch built around a running joke over karaoke and music taste, as the family bickers about whether Stacy is supposed to be at work and whose playlist is better. In between there's some wry, weary commentary about how tiring it is to look after toys who "live for an eternity," before the group settles in for a walk in the park.

title: October Ale and Sparring Practice
synopsis: A slower domestic stretch mixing sword-sparring drills in the training room with everyday family planning: dinner, a trip out for a new CD, and buffalo wings. It ends on a cozy, slightly chaotic bedtime with the older and younger siblings piling into bed, capped by a mishap involving spilled "October ale" landing right on Baby Sam's head.

title: The Unlimiter Breakfast Special
synopsis: A busy breakfast scene built around a mysterious kitchen gadget called the Unlimiter, scrambled eggs, and a debate over Hershey's syrup toppings, all in service of putting together a special plate for Mom on Mother's Day. The kids also negotiate the finer points of skipping school, in classic sibling-logic fashion, while trying not to let anyone burn their tongue on a too-hot treat.

title: Soccer Under Siege
synopsis: With Stacy watching the kids while Tigger and Piglet are off on vacation, the household settles into cheeseburgers for lunch and a game of soccer with a twist: Makuta keeps trying to crash the field, so someone has to hold him off while everyone else plays. A lighter, game-focused stretch punctuated by a quick training-room skirmish against Pa Rock.

title: The Ribbon Horse Story
synopsis: Between cooking dinner and looking after the little ones, Bella improvises a bedtime story for the kids about a farm dog and a family of horses fussed over with colored ribbons and saddles. A rare storytelling-focused episode, gentle and slice-of-life, more about the ritual of settling the kids down than any battle.

title: Bath Time for the Herd
synopsis: The ribbon-horse story wraps up before the episode shifts into a full grooming montage, with shampoo, combs, and careful instructions on how to brush everyone's fur and tails without nicking a whisker. It ends with the kids tucked in and watching TV under Aku Aku's watch, a cozy, low-stakes household routine stretch.

title: The Yooka Call Wake-Up
synopsis: Louie the swan returns from his trip and immediately causes chaos, practicing his trumpet and blowing the "Yooka Call" to rouse the entire household at four in the morning. Between grumbling parents, sword practice, and a game of basketball, the family scrambles to get everyone back to bed, and the stretch closes out the second movie with a group photo and a "see you next time."

title: New Faces, Old Enemy
synopsis: Kicking off the third movie, the narrator introduces a wave of new Super Family members before a familiar emergency hotline call arrives: Makuta has risen again, and this time the team resolves to hit him with everything they've got so he stays down for good. Along the way there's a pet skunk causing trouble at the door and a stash of mysterious "loogie eggs" tucked away in the training room for safekeeping.

title: Bella's Family Strikes First
synopsis: The team heads out to Makuta's lair, carefully avoiding "the basket" trap from last time, and Bella's family gets sent in first to test him. The fight ping-pongs between mask swaps, a meditation stall tactic, and a string of named special moves like the Viper Beam and Mask of Invisitor, with a squirrel companion jumping in partway through.

title: Hyper Beams and the Rowdy Ruff Boys
synopsis: The battle against Makuta escalates as one of the baby heroes piles on with a "final beam" and a "super hyper beam," determined to keep him pinned to the ground. The Powerpuff Girls and Rowdy Ruff Boys crash the fight too, though as the narrator notes, "these guys never talk" -- it's a busy, crowded brawl stretch.

title: Grandma Pikachu Joins the Fight
synopsis: More reinforcements pour into the battle, including Grandma Pikachu, a duo working a blaster, and a pair of fighters who compare the brawl to a battle from a favorite storybook. Even the youngest kids land a devastating hit, and Makuta starts to visibly crack under the combined assault.

title: Enter the Toa
synopsis: A short, fast-moving stretch as the extended family keeps landing hits, a buzz saw attack, a fire burst, a confusion move, while Makuta insists nobody can defeat him. The segment ends on a cliffhanger beat as the Toa themselves finally arrive to join the fight.

title: The Toa's Mask Arsenal
synopsis: With the Toa now on the scene, the battle turns into a showcase of swapped masks, night vision, x-ray vision, strength, and more, as each hero cycles through powers to try to get an edge on Makuta. There's some clever back-and-forth about Makuta reading the heroes' "secret talk" to predict their attacks, keeping the fight tense as it stays firmly mid-battle by episode's end.

title: Never Say Die, Makuta
synopsis: Masks fly fast as Conra and the Toa gang up on Makuta, swapping vision masks, invisibility masks, and confusion tricks mid-fight. Between blows, the narrator lays down the rules of this universe: nobody in the Super Family ever really dies, they just get knocked out and heal back up. The battle turns gross and goofy when a creature chomps a hero's whole head off, chews for a while, and spits him back out none the worse for wear.

title: To Be Continued On Tape Two
synopsis: A quick, scrappy mask battle plays out with illusions, kicks, and a lot of trash talk, including a hero who admits he's secretly been keeping his loyalties quiet. Just as things get interesting, the narrator breaks the fourth wall to explain the story is too big for one tape and has to continue on tape two.

title: The Bohrok-Va Strike Back
synopsis: A fresh wave of Bohrok-Va roll in against Makuta, each one boasting about its krana and its shielding powers before getting knocked around. The heroes trade quips about who's the toughest as they pick krana and masks off one enemy after another, working their way through the swarm one bug at a time.

title: Secret of the Exo-Toa
synopsis: More Bohrok-Va pile into the fight, flinging krana, magnetizing, and unleashing elemental attacks as the battle grinds on. In a quiet moment, one of the heroes finally spills the secret they've been sitting on: to beat all twelve Bohrok swarms, the Toa and Turaga are going to need a giant robot called the Exo-Toa.

title: Solar Beams and Krana Strikes
synopsis: The battle gets a strange new flavor as the heroes start calling out solar beams, thunderbolts, and confusion attacks against a stubborn krana-wearing foe. It takes a barrage of hits and a super confusion combo to finally wear the enemy down and knock its last krana loose.

title: Doctor Senor's Vow of Vengeance
synopsis: With krana knocked loose and Bohrok defeated one by one, Doctor Senor steps up to deliver a full battlefield speech, swearing vengeance for everyone Makuta has killed. It's part victory lap, part declaration of war, ending with a promise that Makuta and every last Bohrok swarm will be wiped out for good.

title: The Slick and Slippery Defense
synopsis: Doctor Senor rolls out a new battle suit and a signature move built entirely around being too slick and slippery to bite, frustrating Makuta's attacks. The fight becomes a showcase of hidden strength, with Doctor Senor claiming he'd only been fighting at partial power the whole time before cutting loose.

title: Sons of a Cruel Father
synopsis: The battle turns into a gut-punch reveal: Makuta has been enslaving and battling his own sons, Conra and Muraka, treating them as disposable weapons. After a furious confrontation and a combined spirit-bomb attack, the sons are rebuilt, forgiven, and offered a place with the good guys. The episode winds down with the toy war fading into ordinary family life, dinner, and homework back at the house.

title: Breakfast, Chores, and a Fake Makuta
synopsis: Between made-up chores, trash duty, and tree-climbing, the household slowly wakes up while everyone waits on Stacey to get moving. The morning ends with a small mask battle against a stand-in Makuta, mostly just to give somebody something to do before breakfast is ready.

title: The Mask Painting Marathon
synopsis: A long, meditative stretch of narration walks through painting toy masks in every color combination imaginable, gold, silver, green, Toa Kaita colors, and beyond. It's mostly quiet hands-on tinkering rather than battle, closing out with a sign-off message from Doctor Senor teasing the next video, 'Beware the Bohrok.'
